exceptions.reason: `Drawer.swipe.test.ts` tests the content: a mouse press in it starts no swipe, so a person selects its text, and a touch there still swipes. `Drawer.Content` marks the press in its own listener and writes no attribute, so the case about the attribute of the content has no counterpart.
`Drawer.test.ts` tests the indent background: it has `data-active` while a drawer of the provider is open.

`Drawer.test.ts` tests the indent: it has `data-active` while a drawer of the provider is open, and the progress of the swipe in `--drawer-swipe-progress`. `Drawer.swipe.test.ts` tests that progress in a swipe that opens.

`Drawer.test.ts` tests the provider: the indent parts are active while a drawer is open and not after its close, and they render with no provider. `Drawer.hydration.test.ts` tests that the provider is not active in the server HTML. The registry cases are internal forms of React: the provider counts the open roots of a reactive set.

`Drawer.test.ts` tests the popup: its role and attributes, the first focus on the popup element and `initialFocus`, the negative snap point offset of a drawer that closes up, the count and the heights of nested drawers, a dialog in a drawer that is no nested drawer, and the error for a popup with no viewport. The popup throws in place of a warning. The cases about the order of React effects and the owner stack have no counterpart.

`Drawer.test.ts` tests the root: the dialog behavior, the handle, the snap point events and the order of the events at a close, the back gesture of Android, and a drawer that counts as a dialog for a dialog. `Drawer.swipe.test.ts` tests the swipe with its threshold and its speed, the snap points of a swipe, a cancelled close and a parent that keeps the drawer open. A snap point change comes after `update:open` at a close. The store and the effect order of React have no counterpart.

`snap.test.ts` tests the heights of the snap points: the units, the values with no height, the clamp, the last of two equal heights, an empty list and a popup with no height. `Drawer.test.ts` tests the offset of a point on the popup. A drawer has a viewport, so the case for a drawer with no viewport has no counterpart, and `KeepAlive` needs no code.
`snap.test.ts` tests the movement past the open place as a square root, and the nearest point.

`Drawer.swipe.test.ts` tests the swipe area: the open at 1 px with the area as the trigger, the popup that follows the finger from its closed place, the release, a release outside the popup that closes nothing, a disabled area, an area that becomes inert, no text selection and the focus that stays, and a swipe while the popup of the last close leaves: the popup enters at the place of the finger after the leave. The Indent has the progress of the Backdrop. Pointer Events carry the swipe, so the cases about touch events and compatibility pointer events have no counterpart.

`Drawer.swipe.test.ts` tests the swipe of the viewport: the release, the square root against the direction, a fast flick, the leave from the place of the drag with `data-swipe-dismiss`, a cancelled close, the elements where a mouse starts no swipe, no text selection, the press of another button, a render in a swipe, a popup that goes, a nested drawer, a listener that stops the press, the snap points, and with a real touch in Chromium: a scroller at its edge and not, a drag across the axis, a touch that starts outside the popup, a `touchmove` listener in the popup, a range input and a selection. The `touchmove` listener is on the viewport element. Pointer Events carry the swipe, so the cases about the touch path, a non-cancelable `touchmove` and the order of React effects have no counterpart.

`Drawer.keyboard.test.tsx` has the cases of the keyboard provider with the new parts. A popup that leaves is a closed popup with `keepMounted`, a tap gets its `click` as a `PointerEvent`, and the inset has no value while no keyboard covers the view. Vue writes a bound `padding-bottom` again at a render, so the docs say to bind none on the scroll body, and the provider keeps no observer of the style (`test/measurements/drawer.test.ts`). `KeepAlive` needs no code.

`Drawer.spec.ts` tests the types of the handle, the props of the root and the trigger, the details of the two change events, the snap point, the element of a template ref and the payload in the slot of the root.

A template ref of the root has `close()`. To keep the popup until a JavaScript animation ends, give `:css="false"` to the `<Transition>` around it, and call `done` in its `leave` hook.

The portal is a `<Teleport>` and renders no element, so it has no `as` and no `element` slot. Put an element in the portal when you need one.

A `<Transition>` around the backdrop animates it, in place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and the `transitionStatus` of the state. A closed backdrop leaves the DOM, or has `[hidden]` with `keepMounted`, so it needs no `data-open` and `data-closed`.

A `<Transition>` around the popup animates it, in place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and the `transitionStatus` of the state. A closed popup leaves the DOM, or has `[hidden]` with `keepMounted`, so it needs no `data-open` and `data-closed`. `[data-swipe-dismiss]` and `[data-swipe-direction]` with the leave class select the leave after a swipe.

The viewport is new in the DOM at each open, so a CSS animation on it runs at the open. `:has(> .v-leave-active)` selects it while its popup leaves, and `[hidden]` while `keepMounted` keeps it closed. These take the place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style`, `data-open`, `data-closed` and the `transitionStatus` of the state.
